reviewer: Pickle: official-source winter camping heater and carbon monoxide safety comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. NEMA/NFA policy briefing (korea.kr, 2024-01-30) National Fire Agency experiment: 119 reports for tent CO poisoning 114 cases over 2019-2022 with 6 cardiac arrests; dome tent hit the 500ppm measurement ceiling in 45 seconds; living-type tent wood firefront 90s/inner 510s, charcoal 70s/180s; gas and kerosene appliances stayed under the 50ppm CO occupational limit but CO2 surged to 45,000ppm (4.5 percent) within a 1-hour experiment; 3 percent CO2 raises heart rate and blood pressure, 5 percent causes dizziness, headache and breathing difficulty, 8 percent unconsciousness or death; CO alarms reacted fastest at the tent ceiling. Yonhap (2024-01-17): 400ppm causes headache in 1-2 hours and 1,600ppm can kill within 2 hours (Korea Gas Safety Corp). KGS (kgs.or.kr): CO symptom table 0.02-1.28 percent with 50ppm occupational limit and emergency procedure. MIOST SafeTV (2024-11-07): kerosene heater inside a tent triggered the alarm at 990ppm after 10 minutes. MIOST policy news (2023-11-09): avoid tent heaters, sleeping bag and hot-water bottle for overnight warmth, if unavoidable ventilate constantly and carry a portable CO alarm. Korea Consumer Agency test (2018-11-21): 8 kerosene camping heaters (wick type, open natural-draft, fuel consumption 600 g/h or less), 4 of 8 failed the 10-second tip-over extinguish requirement (EL safety standard annex 71), all 8 passed CO 0.07 percent or less; CISS records 25 injury cases, 10 (40 percent) fire or burn. Consumer Agency camping gas-leak alarm survey (Yonhap, 2025-03-06): 13 of 15 (86.7 percent) failed alarm or sound levels; statutory alarm stages 55ppm within 60-90 min, 110ppm within 10-40 min, 330ppm within 3 min, 70dB minimum; portable camping units outside the scope; NFA camping gas-poisoning calls rose from 39 (2022) to 64 (2023). KBS (2025-01-24) KGS live test: about 150 camping gas-poisoning accidents and 27 deaths in the recent 3 years; portable gas heater in a 2-3 person tent reached 1,600ppm in 15 minutes. Yonhap News TV (2024-10-22) NFA: 596 camping accident dispatches last year, falls 34 percent, 11 of 15 cardiac arrests caused by gas poisoning in enclosed spaces. Tourism Promotion Act Enforcement Rule annex 7 (current 2025-12-29 edition via law.go.kr download flSeq=159740597): enclosed movable camping tents may use only safety-certified electric products totaling 1,100 W or less when the campground has a leakage breaker; operator-provided camping facilities must have extinguisher, standalone smoke alarm, CO alarm and dedicated breaker; wood and pellet stoves banned in operator facilities. Amendment note (MCST Ordinance 622, effective 2025-12-29) raised the tent electric limit from 600 W to 1,100 W. KGS director interview (Energy News, 2022-10-18): alarms trigger at 250ppm, mount near the ceiling, use KFI product-inspection pass items; lodging facilities must install CO alarms since 2020-08-05. Korea National Park Service campground notice (2024-11-17): combustion appliances including kerosene heaters, fan heaters and no-ignition heaters banned in national park campgrounds. Product pages verified in-browser on 2026-11-01: Paseco CAMP-10 SUNSET convection kerosene heater 199,000 KRW (42 percent off 349,000), 127 reviews, 4.7L tank, KC B713H001-6001G, product 9275515027-27457288377; Shinil kerosene fan heater SFH-BH900 wow price 379,050 KRW (36 percent off 599,000, regular 399,000 at 33 percent), 45 reviews, thermostat control, tank 9L, KC B713R002-6001C, product 9619638258-28725112452; Soosan Hometech COB-380V digital CO alarm 24,650 KRW (10 percent off 27,500), 422 reviews, national test BEQJ 89395 (2024-47), product 6911591845-24956693249, existing affiliate deep link reused. Affiliate short links for ranks 1-2 freshly issued from Coupang Partners AF6593875 (ij40Kw0F2W, ij43bA4AmW); rank 3 reuses verified link iejzl436ia. Derived calculations recorded in research: full BEST-3 setup 602,700 KRW (627,350 KRW with a second alarm), tank capacity 9L is about 1.9x of 4.7L. Plan deviations: the plan's headline 600W campground rule was updated to the current 1,100W statutory limit with the 2025-12-29 amendment cited and campground-specific lower caps noted; the plan's numbered per-hour kerosene consumption figures could not be verified in primary sources, so the guide uses the Consumer Agency 600 g/h class and tank-capacity comparison instead; plan's product 2 title said 'camping/indoor fan heater (600W compatible, auto-extinguish)' - the actual best-selling Shinil fan heater SFH-BH900 is a kerosene fan heater with thermostat control, so the mapping uses the verified product and its real specs.
